extracted.intended_audience: businesses and legal counsel offering negative-option/subscription products, trade associations, regulatory analysts, and agency staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required analytical elements for complying with and analyzing the FTC's final Rule on negative option features (disclosures, consent, cancellations, recordkeeping), and the agency's economic/PRA/FRFA analyses supporting the Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misrepresentations in marketing negative option features
rubrics_metrics.description: The final Rule prohibits sellers from misrepresenting material facts in connection with promoting or offering for sale a good or service with a negative option feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes marketing claims tied to negative option features; enforcement may include civil penalties under the Rule. The Commission cited widespread deceptive/unfair practices (material misrepresentations, failure to provide important terms prior to charging, lack of informed consent, and failure to provide a simple cancellation method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material terms immediately adjacent to consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must disclose certain important information about negative option features, and the Commission limits the number of terms that must appear 'immediately adjacent' to the request for consent to the negative option feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission defined 'material' and provided concrete categories of material facts to clarify interpretation. The change narrows mandatory adjacent disclosure items compared to the NPRM to reduce burden while ensuring consumers receive key information before giving billing info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain express informed consent and maintain records
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must obtain a consumer's express informed consent to the negative option feature and maintain records of consumer consent for three years after the initial transaction unless the seller satisfies the technological exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Rule provides an alternative compliance option so sellers can avoid retaining consent records if they have requisite processes in place. The Commission fixed retention to three years (shorter than some proposals) to limit burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a simple mechanism for cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sellers must provide consumers a simple mechanism for cancellation of negative option plans, including honoring cancellation requests, not denying refunds when appropriate, and not forcing consumers to cancel by a different method than used to enroll.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Rule targets practices such as requiring refunds only upon return of unordered goods, forcing payment to return goods, or requiring a different cancellation channel than enrollment. The Commission assumes providing alternative cancellation paths (phone/online) imposes limited costs for firms that previously offered only in-person/mail cancellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and definition of covered entities and 'negative option'
rubrics_metrics.description: The final Rule applies to sellers engaged in making negative option offers, defined as any person 'selling, offering, charging for, or otherwise marketing goods or services with a Negative Option Feature.' The Commission narrowed scope by excluding persons solely 'promoting' negative option plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC staff estimates ~106,000 entities offer negative option features; this estimate is conservative for burden analysis. The scope clarification aims to reduce unnecessary coverage while retaining broad application across industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and staging to reduce burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission delayed the effective date of most final Rule provisions for 180 days to allow implementation, while provisions related to misrepresentations and other procedural requirements take effect 60 days after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staged effective dates are intended to give businesses time to implement reasonable operational and technical changes without immediate enforcement for all provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications to proposed rule to minimize burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to comments, the Commission modified the proposal by defining 'material', limiting immediately-adjacent terms, removing separate affirmative consent to 'the rest of the transaction', modifying recordkeeping, and removing 'saves' and annual 'reminder' requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes were explicitly adopted to reduce recordkeeping and disclosure burdens and to avoid prescriptive requirements that might stifle innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate initial-year compliance costs by component
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial-year compliance costs should be estimated by summing: familiarization costs, disclosure costs, cancellation-mechanism costs, and recordkeeping costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission provides numeric estimates (2023$): Familiarization $35.97–$341.22M; Disclosure $3.96–$39.57M; Cancellation $3.04–$34.93M; Recordkeeping $6.54M; Total Year-1 $49.52–$422.26M. The methodology includes applying per-firm unit costs to estimated counts of affected firms and accounting for fractions already compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break down cancellation costs by baseline cancellation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate cancellation compliance costs by distributing subscriptions/cancellations across baseline enrollment and cancellation methods (online enrollment/online cancellation compliant, online enrollment/online non-compliant, online enrollment/telephone cancellation, telephone enrollment/telephone cancellation, in-person enrollment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission used enforcement and experimental data to assign shares (example from alternative analysis for online enrollments: 18.75% Rule-compliant online; 18.75% require phone; 62.5% non-straightforward online). Cost calculations use per-firm per-action unit costs (e.g., relabeling online elements 1×–8× $45.95; telephonic compliance up to $532.05 per firm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate ongoing compliance costs (Years 2–10) assuming template reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume that once compliant disclosures and cancellation paths are created, they form reusable templates and there are no incremental disclosure or cancellation costs for adding new subscription products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission treats template updates as routine business costs, not incremental compliance costs. It does, however, estimate possible annual compliance-check attorney hours (upper bound 5 hours × wage $84.84) producing an aggregate annual range for compliance checks of $0–$44.97M; inclusive of recordkeeping, annual ongoing costs are $6.54–$51.51M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute present discounted value and annualized costs using a 2% discount rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate present discounted value (PDV) of costs over 10 years and annualize costs using a 2% discount rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission reports PDV over 10 years at 2% of $100.89–$826.15M, and annualized costs of $11.23–$91.97M per year. Apply the same approach for benefits when comparing to costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct sensitivity analysis with alternative baseline assumptions and experimental evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform sensitivity analyses that alter baseline distributions (e.g., share of online vs telephone cancellations) and re-run benefit and cost estimates, using experimental or other empirical evidence to justify alternative shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission's alternative analysis assumed 1.9% phone enrollments (2,000/106,000) and used a 16-subscription experiment (3/16 easy online, 3/16 required phone, 10/16 non-straightforward) to set online cancellation shares. Results produced benefits ranges and differences from main analysis; even with alternative assumptions, benefits exceeded costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider selection bias when using enforcement data versus market data
rubrics_metrics.description: When allocating baseline cancellation methods, weigh the potential selection bias of enforcement case data (resolved cases may be older, reflect egregious violations) and consider alternative sources such as market statistics or experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main analysis used enforcement data; the Commission acknowledges this may under- or over-represent current market practices, so it compares an alternative approach using NPRM statistics plus experiment-derived shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) submission and burden-analysis requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must obtain OMB approval before collecting information from ten or more persons and must include a PRA burden analysis (number of respondents, burden hours, labor/non-labor costs, and justification of necessity/utility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC submitted the final Rule and a Supplemental Supporting Statement to OMB. The NPRM provided burden estimates and solicited comments; the final PRA adopts the NPRM's figures absent contrary evidence. The PRA section must explain methodology and solicit empirical evidence for estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA burden-hour and labor-cost estimation methodology (numbers and wages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate number of respondents, annual burden hours for recordkeeping and disclosures, and associated labor costs using representative wage rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC adopted: 106,000 estimated entities; recordkeeping burden 53,000 entities × 1 hour/yr = 53,000 hrs; disclosure burden = 212,000 hrs (2 hrs per seller on average); labor wage assumptions: $18.75/hr (clerical) for recordkeeping, $22.15/hr (sales personnel) for disclosures; resulting annual labor costs ~$5.69M. Capital/start-up costs assumed de minimis and borne in normal course of business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (FRFA) required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rule could have significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities, the FRFA must include several specified elements (statement of need/objectives; summary and assessment of public comments; response to SBA Chief Counsel; estimate of small entities affected; description of reporting/recordkeeping/compliance requirements and skill needs; steps taken to minimize economic impacts and reasons for rejecting alternatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission performed an FRFA even after certifying no significant impact; the FRFA should describe how public comments were considered, what changes were made to reduce burden (e.g., narrowed scope, limited disclosures, shorter retention), and provide factual/policy/legal reasons for adopted alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative record and burden of proof for contested cost claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When commenters assert higher costs, they must provide empirical evidence or data; in the absence of such evidence, disputed cost estimates may be treated as not genuinely disputed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer found insufficient evidence to resolve disputed recordkeeping/disclosure cost claims when commenters (e.g., IAB, NCTA) provided generalizations but not empirical support. Agencies may adopt NPRM estimates when no contrary evidence is presented.
